Gonadal failure, vitiligo, alopecia, and chronic atrophic gastritis, with or without pernicious anemia, can occur.

qs.q: A patient with suspected pernicious anemia and atrophic gastritis presents with a dimorphic blood picture. Which two deficiencies are most likely co-existing?
qs.e: Pernicious anemia can lead to B12 deficiency which, when combined with iron deficiency (often due to atrophic gastritis affecting iron absorption), results in a dimorphic anemia. Folate and iron deficiency are typically seen in conditions like pregnancy or alcoholism.

qs.q: A 58-year-old woman is evaluated for megaloblastic anaemia and atrophic gastritis limited to the gastric body and fundus. Laboratory studies show hypochlorhydria and hypergastrinaemia. Which autoantibody profile is most characteristic of this condition?
qs.e: Autoimmune metaplastic atrophic gastritis targets the body and fundus, featuring autoantibodies against parietal cells and intrinsic factor. Antinuclear and anti-smooth muscle antibodies are instead typically associated with autoimmune hepatitis.

qs.q: A patient with chronic atrophic gastritis is at risk of which type of anaemia?
qs.e: Atrophic gastritis destroys parietal cells that produce intrinsic factor, impairing B12 absorption and causing pernicious anaemia.
qs.s: Haematology Exam 2025: MCQs on Anaemia, Leukaemia & Clotting
